      <div class="cmp-text ">
        <h3><a id="public-consultations"></a>ASX public consultations</h3>
<h4>2026</h4>

      </div>
    
    
    
    

  </div></div>


    
    
    <div class="table-component">
 
  <div class="table-container paddingtop15 paddingbottom60 normalTable">
    
    <div data-table-fix-col="0" data-table-fix-row="0" class="rebrand-datatables  ''">
        
            <table border="0" width="100%" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="1"><thead></thead><tbody><tr style="	text-align: left;
"><td><b>Date</b></td><td colspan="2" width="90%"><b>Description</b></td></tr><tr><td>30/09/2026</td><td colspan="2"><p>On Wednesday 30 September 2026, ASX published a consultation paper on the <a href="/content/dam/asx/markets/clearing-and-settlement-services/clearstar-program/2026/etd-futures-clearing-replacement-asxclf-operating-rules-and-procedures-consultation-v1.0.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">ASX Clear (Futures) Operating Rules and Procedure Amendments</a>, including <a href="/content/dam/asx/markets/clearing-and-settlement-services/clearstar-program/2026/etd-futures-clearing-replacement-rule-and-procedure-amendments.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">supporting reference document</a>.</p>
<p>The Exchange Traded Derivatives (ETD) Futures Clearing replacement project is part of the ClearStar Program to modernise systems and improve efficiencies of the derivatives clearing business. The consultation paper provides information on proposed amendments to the ASX Clear (Futures) Operating Rules and Procedures required to support the replacement of the existing Genium futures clearing platform. There are also minor clarification changes to the ASX 24 Operating Rules. This paper is intended for ASX Clear (Futures) Clearing Participants, ASX 24 Trading Participants, software providers, service providers, industry associations, and other stakeholders involved in futures clearing.</p>
<p>ASX welcomes market submissions on proposals and questions outlined in the consultation paper. One written submission is requested per organisation by Friday 30 October 2026, via email to <a href="mailto:ASXClearStar&#64;asx.com.au" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">ASXClearStar&#64;asx.com.au</a>.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td rowspan="2">18/09/2026</td><td colspan="2"><p>On Friday 18 September 2026, ASX released its <a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/shareholder-approval-of-dilutive-acquisitions-and-changes-in-admission-status-consultation-response.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">response to feedback</a> received on the consultation on the exposure draft Listing Rules and Guidance Notes amendments concerning shareholder approval of dilutive acquisitions and changes in admission status, published on Wednesday 17 June 2026.</p>
<p>The June 2026 consultation paper focused on four main areas:</p>
<ul><li>that the operation and interactions of the draft amendments with other ASX Listing Rules or Guidance Notes ensure the amended framework operates clearly, consistently and as intended;</li><li>that the key definitions and concepts in the draft amendments are clear, objective and administrable;</li><li>whether post approval issuance periods following shareholder approvals for issuing securities should be standardised to a 12 month period; and</li><li>a commencement date of the amended Listing Rules and Guidance Notes of Wednesday 21 October 2026, and transitional provisions that may support this date.</li></ul>
<p>The response paper summarises the feedback received and sets out ASX’s proposed way forward on the four areas, including the final amendments to the Listing Rules and Guidance Notes that are now subject to completion of the statutory process for amending rules. </p>
<p>Subject to completion of the statutory process for amending rules, the amended Listing Rules and Guidance Notes will come into effect on Wednesday 21 October 2026. </p>
<p>ASX will release a Market Notice to confirm the completion of the statutory process. </p>
<p>ASX received 12 submissions in response to the June 2026 consultation paper from a broad cross-section of market participants, including asset managers, industry bodies, law firms and investment banks. All non-confidential submissions are available below: </p>
</td></tr><tr><td><ul><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/australian-council-of-superannuation-investors-20260918.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Australian Council of Superannuation Investors</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/australiansuper-20260918.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">AustralianSuper</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/blackwall-legal-20260918.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Blackwall Legal</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/governance-institute-of-australia-20260918.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Governance Institute of Australia</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/ifm-investors-20260918.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">IFM Investors</a></li></ul>
</td><td><ul><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/law-council-of-australia-20260918.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Law Council of Australia</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/mccabes-20260918.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">McCabes</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/ownership-matters-20260918.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Ownership Matters</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/stockbrokers-and-investment-advisers-association-20260918.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Stockbrokers and Investment Advisers Association (SIAA)</a></li></ul>
</td></tr><tr><td>1/09/2026</td><td colspan="2">ASX has made available a recording of the <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v&#61;_30z0f0wa6A&amp;t&#61;9s">ASX and Advisory Group on Corporate Governance public briefing session</a>, recorded on Tuesday 18 August 2026 in Sydney, about the draft 5th edition ASX Corporate Principles and Recommendations (Principles) that is open for public consultation until Monday 14 September 2026.</td></tr><tr><td>17/08/2026</td><td colspan="2"><p>On Monday 17 August 2026, ASX released its <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/tpc-response-to-consultation-and-appendix-20260817.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">response paper</a> on the January 2026 <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/260116-tpc-consultation-paper-and-appendix.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">ASX Clear Third Party Clearing Capital Requirements and Other Proposed Amendments consultation paper</a>.</p>
<p>ASX received five written submissions in response to the consultation paper, four of which were provided on a confidential basis. The submission provided on a non-confidential basis is available at the link below:</p>
<ul><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/siaa-consultation-feedback-20260227.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Stockbrokers and Investment Advisers Association (SIAA)</a></li></ul>
</td></tr><tr><td>21/07/2026</td><td colspan="2"><p>On Tuesday 21 July 2026, ASX released its consultation paper on the draft 5<sup>th</sup> edition of the ASX Corporate Governance Principles and Recommendations (Principles).</p>
<p>The consultation paper outlines proposed changes to the Principles 4<sup>th</sup> edition; and consequential changes to the ASX Listing Rules and Guidance Notes, including Appendix 4G – Key to disclosures.</p>
<p>To support the consultation, ASX has included the following documents:</p>
<ul><li>a <a target="_blank" href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/media-releases/2026/21-july-media-release-asx-updated-corporate-governance-principles.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Media Release</a>;</li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/corporate-governance-council/asx-corporate-governance-principles-and-recommendations-draft-5th-edition-consultation-paper.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Consultation Paper: ASX Corporate Governance Principles and Recommendations – Draft 5<sup>th</sup> edition</a>;</li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/corporate-governance-council/annexure-a-asx-corporate-governance-principles-and-recommendations-5th-edition-consultation.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Annexure A: 5<sup>th</sup> edition ASX Corporate Governance Principles and Recommendations – Consultation Draft</a>; and</li><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/corporate-governance-council/annexure-b-proposed-consequential-changes-to-the-asx-listing-rules-and-guidance-notes.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Annexure B: Draft ASX Listing Rule amendments and Guidance Notes</a>.</li></ul>
<p>The following documents may assist stakeholders navigate the proposed changes from the 4th edition to the 5th edition:</p>
<ul><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/corporate-governance-council/roadmap-of-recommendation-changes.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Roadmap of recommendation changes</a>; and</li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/corporate-governance-council/mark-up-of-the-draft-principles-and-recommendations-in-the-5th-edition-against-the-4th-edition.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">A mark-up of the Draft Principles, against the 4<sup>th</sup> edition’s principles and recommendations</a>.</li></ul>
<p>ASX is seeking submissions on the questions set out in the Consultation Paper. Written submissions are requested by 5.00pm AEST on Monday, 14 September 2026.  Electronic submissions should be sent to <a href="mailto:ListingsPolicy&#64;asx.com.au">ListingsPolicy&#64;asx.com.au</a>.</p>
<p>In August, ASX will also host public forums in Sydney, Brisbane, Melbourne, Adelaide and Perth where members of ASX and the ASX’s Advisory Group on Corporate Governance will speak and answer questions about the draft 5<sup>th</sup> edition of the Principles. If you are interested in attending, please register via the following links:</p>
<ul><li><a href="https://event.asx.com.au/corporategovernancebriefingsydaug2026" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Sydney, 18 August 2026 - 9.30-10.30am</a>;</li><li><a href="https://event.asx.com.au/corporategovernancebriefingbrisaug2026" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Brisbane, 19 August 2026 – 9.30-10.30am</a>;</li><li><a href="https://event.asx.com.au/corporategovernancebriefingmelbaug26" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Melbourne, 21 August 2026 – 9.30-10.30am</a>;</li><li><a href="https://event.asx.com.au/corporategovernancebriefingadeaug2026" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Adelaide, 25 August 2026 – 9.30-10.30am</a>; and</li><li><a href="https://event.asx.com.au/corporategovernancebriefingperaug2026" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Perth, 27 August 2026 – 9.30-10.30am</a>.</li></ul>
<p>For those who cannot attend, the Sydney event will be recorded and this webpage updated with the recording once available.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td rowspan="3">17/06/2026</td><td colspan="2"><p>On Wednesday 17 June 2026, ASX released its <a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/response-to-public-consultation-on-shareholder-approval-of-dilutive-acquisitions-and-changes-in-admission-status.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">response to consultation feedback received</a> in relation to the <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2025/public-consultation-on-shareholder-approval-requirements-under-the-asx-listings-rules.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">consultation on Shareholder approval of dilutive acquisitions and changes in admission status</a>, which was published on 20 October 2025.</p>
<p>The October 2025 consultation paper focused on four main areas:</p>
<ul><li>the issue of shares under a regulated takeover or merger</li><li>when a dual listed company wants to change to ASX Foreign Exempt Listing status</li><li>when a dual listed company proposes to delist from the ASX</li><li>significant changes to the nature or scale of a listed company’s activities.</li></ul>
<p>The response paper summarises the feedback received and sets out ASX’s proposed way forward on the four areas, including an exposure draft of proposed Listing Rule amendments relating to:</p>
<ul><li>changes in admission status</li><li>voluntary delistings</li><li>issue of shares under a regulated takeover or merger.</li></ul>
<p>ASX is seeking submissions on the questions set out in the response paper. Written submissions are requested by 5.00pm AEST on Wednesday 29 July 2026. Electronic submissions should be sent to <a target="_blank" href="mailto:ListingsPolicy&#64;asx.com.au" rel="noopener noreferrer">ListingsPolicy&#64;asx.com.au</a>.</p>
<p>ASX received 45 submissions in response to the October 2025 consultation paper from a broad cross-section of market participants, including asset managers, industry bodies, law firms, investment banks and listed entities. All non-confidential submissions are available below:</p>
</td></tr><tr><td><ul><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/acsi-response-to-consultation-paper-20260617.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">ACSI</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/airlie-funds-management-response-to-consultation-paper-20260617.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Airlie Funds Management</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/allan-gray-australia-pty-ltd-response-to-consultation-paper-20260617.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Allan Gray Australia Pty Ltd</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/asfa-response-to-consultation-paper-20260617.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">ASFA</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/ashurst-response-to-consultation-paper-20260617.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Ashurst</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/aicd-response-to-consultation-paper-20260617.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Australian Institute of Company Directors</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/art-response-to-consultation-paper-20260617.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Australian Retirement Trust</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/asa-response-to-consultation-paper-20260617.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Australian Shareholders&#39; Association</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/australiansuper-response-to-consultation-paper-20260617.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">AustralianSuper</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/barrenjoey-response-to-consultation-paper-20260617.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Barrenjoey</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/cbus-response-to-consultation-paper-20260617.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Cbus</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/chapman-tripp-response-to-consultation-paper-20260617.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Chapman Tripp</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/dimensional-fund-advisors-response-to-consultation-paper-20260617.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Dimensional Fund Advisors</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/dla-piper-response-to-consultation-paper-20260617.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">DLA Piper</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/gia-response-to-consultation-paper-20260617.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Governance Institute of Australia</a></li><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/hesta-response-to-consultation-paper-20260617.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Hesta</a></li></ul>
</td><td><ul><li><a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/ifm-investors-response-to-consultation-paper-20260617.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">IFM noreferrer">WaveStone Capital</a></li></ul>
</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Please direct any queries regarding the consultation to <a target="_blank" href="mailto:ListingsPolicy&#64;asx.com.au" rel="noopener noreferrer">ListingsPolicy&#64;asx.com.au</a>.</td></tr><tr><td>31/03/2026</td><td colspan="2"><p>On Tuesday 31 March 2026, ASX released its <a href="/content/dam/asx/markets/clearing-and-settlement-services/public-consultation-feedback-response-asxclf-dynamic-defualt-fund.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">response</a> to consultation feedback received in relation to the consultation paper titled ASX Clear (Futures) Dynamic Default Fund Framework.</p>
<p>The consultation paper was published on 21 July 2025. </p>
<p>The Response summarises the feedback received, provides ASX’s position on those matters and the changes to the rule amendments that ASX intends to make in response to the feedback received. </p>
<p>ASX received 2 non-confidential submissions and 7 confidential submissions feedback. Non-confidential submissions were received from the following respondents:</p>
<ul><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/markets/clearing-and-settlement-services/asxcf-dynamic-df-framework-isda-response.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">ISDA</a></li><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/markets/clearing-and-settlement-services/asx-dynamic-default-fund-consultation-fia-response.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">FIA</a></li></ul>
<p>ASX appreciates the time and effort of all stakeholders who provided feedback.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>30/03/2026</td><td colspan="2"><p>On Monday 30 March 2026, ASX released its <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/consultation-paper-response-closure-of-mfund-march-2026.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">response paper</a> to the <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2025/mfund-consultation-paper-on-proposed-rule-amendments.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Consultation of the closure of the ASX Managed Fund Settlement Service (mFund)</a>.</p>
<p>ASX did not receive any formal submissions to the Consultation Paper.</p>
<p>The response outlines additional proposed amendments to the ASX Operating Rules and ASX Settlement Operating Rules to support the closure of mFund. The amendments include the removal of rules and terms specific to mFund, and introduce transitional arrangements that will facilitate a fair and orderly wind down. The amendments also include the closure of the AQUA Quote Display Board (AQDB).</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>26/02/2026</td><td colspan="2">On Thursday 26 February, ASX released its <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/asx-24-response-to-consultation-on-aot-20260226.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">response paper</a> summarising feedback in relation to the consultation paper on Anomalous Order Thresholds (AOT) on ASX 24 products.</td></tr><tr><td>16/01/2026</td><td colspan="2"><p>On Friday 16 January 2026, ASX released a <a></a><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/260116-tpc-consultation-paper-and-appendix.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">consultation paper</a> titled ASX Clear Third Party Clearing Capital Requirements and Other Proposed Amendments.</p>
<p>The consultation paper outlines proposed changes resulting from a review of the capital requirements for third party clearers (TPCs), namely:</p>
<ul><li>changes to the base requirement component of the core requirement for capital to be held by TPCs; and</li><li>the recognition of security deposits collected from trading participants and intermediaries as collateral to reduce counterparty risk amounts.</li></ul>
<p>In addition, the paper includes proposals relating to daily or weekly reporting which are separate from the TPC review.</p>
<p>ASX welcomes feedback from stakeholders on the consultation and supporting rule amendments. Written submissions are requested by 27 February 2026.</p>
</td></tr></tbody></table>

"><td><b>Date</b></td><td width="90%"><b>Description</b></td></tr><tr><td>19/12/2025</td><td><p>On Friday 19 December 2025, ASX Limited and ASX Settlement Pty Limited (together ASX) released its consultation paper titled <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2025/mfund-consultation-paper-on-proposed-rule-amendments.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Consultation of the closure of the ASX Managed Fund Settlement Service</a>.</p>
<p>This consultation follows the announcement made on 27 November 2023 that ASX has decided to wind down and close the ‘ASX Managed Fund Settlement Service’ (mFund).</p>
<p>ASX seeks stakeholder feedback on proposed amendments to the ASX Operating Rules and ASX Settlement Operating Rules to support the closure of mFund. The proposed amendments include the removal of rules and terms specific to mFund and, introduce transitional arrangements that will facilitate a fair and orderly wind down. The consultation also contemplates proposed amendments to the ASX Operating Rules to support the closure of the AQUA Quote Display Board (AQDB).</p>
<p>Written submissions are requested by Thursday 12 February 2026.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>19/12/2025</td><td><p> </p>
<p>On Friday 19 December 2025, ASX <a href="/content/dam/asx/documents/listings/supervision-updates/2025/listed-at-asx-compliance-update-19-december-2025.pdf">confirmed</a> that it will proceed with an amendment to Listing Rule 17.5, which will become effective on 16 January 2026, subject to regulatory approvals.</p>
<p>The amendment was proposed in a consultation paper titled <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2025/amendment-to-listing-rule-17.5-consultation-paper.pdf">Amendment to Listing Rule 17.5</a>, published on 31 October 2025.<u><br />
</u></p>
<p>ASX received eight submissions from a range of stakeholders, including listed entities, industry associations and professional services firms. Non-confidential submissions were received from the following respondents:</p>
<ul><li><a></a><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2025/aira-response-to-amendment-to-listing-rule-17.5-consultation-paper.pdf">Australasian Investor Relations Association</a></li><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2025/ca-anz-response-amendment-to-listing-rule-17.5-consultation-paper.pdf">Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand</a></li><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2025/law-council-of-australia-response-amendment-to-listing-rule-17.5-consultation-paper.pdf">Corporations Committee of the Business Law Section of the Law Council of Australia</a></li><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2025/deloitte-response-amendment-to-listing-rule-17.5-consultation-paper.pdf">Deloitte</a></li><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2025/gia-response-amendment-to-listing-rule-17.5-consultation-paper.pdf">Governance Institute of Australia</a></li><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2025/nexia-australia-response-amendment-to-listing-rule-17.5-consultation-paper.pdf">Nexia Australia</a></li><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2025/wembley-corporate-services-response-amendment-to-listing-rule-17.5-consultation-paper.pdf">Wembley Corporate Services</a></li></ul>

</td></tr><tr><td>17/12/2025</td><td><p>On Wednesday 17 December, ASX released its <a href="/content/dam/asx/markets/clearing-and-settlement-services/response-to-feedback-on-proposed-introduction-of-fees-for-cdn.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">response</a> to stakeholder feedback received in relation to the discussion paper <a href="/content/dam/asx/markets/clearing-and-settlement-services/discussion-paper-proposed-introduction-of-fees-for-chess-depositary-nominee-services-for-cdi-issuers.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Proposed introduction of fees for CHESS Depositary Nominee Services for CDI Issuers</a> which was published on 21 August 2025.</p>

</td></tr><tr><td>31/10/2025</td><td><p>On 31 October 2025, ASX released its consultation paper titled <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2025/amendment-to-listing-rule-17.5-consultation-paper.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Amendment to Listing Rule 17.5</a>.</p>
<p>Listing Rule 17.5 provides that trading in a listed entity’s securities will be suspended if the entity fails to lodge the annual reporting documents required under Listing Rule 4.5 by the due date.</p>
<p>The Corporations Act was recently amended to require some entities to prepare annual sustainability reports. This amendment to the Corporations Act has the flow on effect that the scope of Listing Rule 17.5 is expanded to require suspension of the securities of listed entities that lodge their sustainability report after the due date (to the extent that they are required to prepare those reports under the new Corporations Act requirements).</p>
<p>ASX is consulting on a proposed change to Listing Rule 17.5 which will have the effect that the late lodgement of an annual sustainability report will not result in mandatory suspension. This is a consequential amendment which is intended to preserve the current status quo following the changes to the Corporations Act.</p>
<p>Written submissions are requested by Friday 28 November 2025. </p>
</td></tr><tr><td>20/10/2025</td><td><p>On 20 October 2025, ASX released its consultation paper titled <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2025/public-consultation-on-shareholder-approval-requirements-under-the-asx-listings-rules.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Shareholder approval of dilutive acquisitions and changes in admission status</a>.</p>
<p>The consultation paper focuses on four main areas, which are:</p>
<ul><li>the issue of shares under a regulated takeover or merger</li><li>when a dual listed company wants to change to ASX Foreign Exempt Listing status</li><li>when a dual listed company proposes to delist from the ASX</li><li>significant changes to the nature or scale of a listed company’s activities.</li></ul>
<p>ASX is seeking submissions on the issues set out in the consultation paper. We encourage stakeholders to provide their feedback on the issues being raised, even if they agree with the initial views ASX has provided on each area.</p>
<p>Written submissions in response to the consultation paper are requested by 5.00pm AEDT on Monday 15 December 2025. Electronic submissions should be sent to <a href="mailto:ListingsPolicy&#64;asx.com.au" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">ListingsPolicy&#64;asx.com.au</a>.</p>
<p>ASX will consider the submissions provided in response to the consultation paper and then prepare and publish a consultation response summarising the feedback that we receive and advising of our proposed way forward.</p>
<p>If the consultation results in specific proposals to amend the Listing Rules, we will also publish an exposure draft of the proposed amendments and invite submissions on those.</p>
<p>The response to consultation and any potential associated exposure draft rule changes are expected to be published in the first half of 2026.</p>
<p>Please direct any queries regarding the consultation paper to <a href="mailto:ListingsPolicy&#64;asx.com.au" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">ListingsPolicy&#64;asx.com.au</a>.</p>

</td></tr><tr><td>21/07/2025</td><td><p>On 21 July 2025, ASX released a <a title="asxclf-dynamic-default-fund-public-consultation-paper" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2025/asxclf-dynamic-default-fund-public-consultation-paper.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">consultation paper</a> titled ASX Clear (Futures) Dynamic Default Fund Framework.</p>
<p>The consultation paper invites feedback on the design and implementation of a Dynamic Default Fund Framework for ASX Clear (Futures). The proposed dynamic framework is a significant change from the existing ASX Clear (Futures) fixed Default Fund and would result in the size of the Default Fund and Clearing Participant variable commitments being recalculated on a monthly basis (subject to a total Default Fund floor of $650M and cap of $1.3B). ASX would continue to contribute $450M to the total Default Fund and commit a tranche ahead of the Default Fund contribution of Clearing Participants sized at 20% of the total Default Fund. ASX also proposes to make changes to replenishment obligations and recovery assessments to align with the introduction of the Dynamic Default Fund.</p>
<p>ASX welcomes feedback from stakeholders on the design of the Dynamic Default Fund and supporting rule amendments. Written submissions are requested by 1 September 2025. </p>

</td></tr><tr><td>15/04/2025</td><td><p>On 15 April 2025, ASX released a consultation paper titled <a href="/content/dam/asx/markets/clearing-and-settlement-services/consultation-paper-for-asx-settlement-operating-rule-amendments-depositary-nominee-services.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">ASX Settlement Operating Rule amendments - Depositary Nominee services</a>.</p>

</td></tr><tr><td>31/03/2025</td><td><p>On 31 March 2025, ASX released a consultation paper titled <a href="/content/dam/asx/markets/clearing-and-settlement-services/clearstar-program/consultation-paper-for-etd-tradeaccept-system-replacement-mar-2025.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Consultation Paper on ETD TradeAccept System Replacement – Off Market Trade Reporting Service</a>.</p>
<p>The Exchange Traded Derivatives (ETD) TradeAccept replacement project is part of the ClearStar Program that looks to modernise systems and improve efficiencies of the derivatives business. The new solution will offer the same or improved business capabilities as the current system, with improved operational efficiencies, extended operating hours, new dashboard management and more enhanced support for automation through system-to-system messaging. This consultation paper outlines the design and scope of the new solution, along with the proposed implementation approach and associated timeline. It is intended for Participants using the TradeAccept system, as well as their system vendors, industry groups, and other stakeholders involved in derivatives off market trade reporting.</p>
<p>ASX welcomes market feedback on proposals and questions outlined in the consultation paper to assist in determining the final solution design and timeline. One written submission is requested per organisation by 30 April 2025, via: </p>
<ul><li>an <a href="/content/dam/asx/markets/clearing-and-settlement-services/clearstar-program/etd-tradeaccept-consultation-response-template.xlsx" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">editable Excel form</a>, submitted by email to <a href="mailto:asxclearstar&#64;asx.com.au" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">ASXClearStar&#64;asx.com.au</a> </li><li>email to <a href="mailto:asxclearstar&#64;asx.com.au" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">ASXClearStar&#64;asx.com.au</a> in a format suitable to your organisation.</li></ul>
</td></tr><tr><td>03/03/2025</td><td><p>On 3 March 2025, ASX released a consultation paper  titled <a href="/content/dam/asx/markets/clearing-and-settlement-services/consultation-on-release-1-clearing-services-amendments-to-rules-and-procedures.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Consultation on Release 1 (Clearing Services) – Amendments to Rules and Procedures</a>. </p>
<p>To facilitate the implementation of Release 1 of CHESS replacement, ASX is required to amend the:</p>
<ol><li>ASX Clear Operating Rules</li><li>ASX Clear Operating Rules Procedures</li><li>ASX Operating Rules Procedures.</li></ol>
<p>The proposed amendments to these rules and procedures reflect the solution design for new or changed functionality in Release 1. </p>
<p>Responses to the consultation paper are requested by 14 April 2025.  </p>
</td></tr><tr><td>03/03/2025</td><td><p>On 3 March 2025, ASX released a consultation paper titled <a href="/content/dam/asx/markets/clearing-and-settlement-services/consultation-on-release-1-clearing-services-amendments-to-amo-contractual-terms.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Consultation on Release 1 (Clearing Services) – Amendments to AMO Contractual Terms</a>. </p>
<p>To facilitate the implementation of Release 1 of CHESS replacement, ASX is required to amend the contractual terms which underpin the services provided by ASX Clear and ASX Settlement to Approved Market Operators (AMOs). The contractual terms (collectively referred to as the ‘AMO Contractual Terms’) include the:</p>
<ol><li>Trade Acceptance Service Legal Terms</li><li>Product Services Legal Terms</li><li>Operational and Technical Standards.</li></ol>
<p>The proposed amendments to the AMO Contractual Terms reflect the solution design for new or changed functionality in Release 1, and also reflect additional amendments included as part of a five-year review process.  </p>
<p>Responses to the consultation paper are requested by 14 April 2025.  </p>
</td></tr></tbody></table>

</td></tr><tr><td>16/09/2024</td><td><p>On 16 September 2024, ASX released a consultation paper titled <a href="/content/dam/asx/markets/clearing-and-settlement-services/asx-pricing-policy-consultation-paper.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Cash Equities Clearing and Settlement Services: Pricing Policy Consultation Paper</a> and an accompanying set of <a href="/content/dam/asx/markets/clearing-and-settlement-services/pricing-policy-questions-and-answers.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Q&amp;A</a>.</p>
<p>This consultation paper proposes to adopt a new pricing policy for ASX’s clearing, settlement and issuer services (‘CS services’) from 1 January 2025. </p>
<p>The cornerstone of the new pricing policy will be the introduction of the Building Block Method (‘BBM’), a widely used pricing model used across regulated industries, to calculate a revenue requirement reflecting the efficient costs of providing our CS services. The pricing policy is designed to ensure, through an annual review, that ASX recovers no more than those costs, including a reasonable return on investment commensurate with the commercial risks involved.</p>
<p>There will be no change to the structure or level of CS services prices upon commencement of the pricing policy. However, the pricing policy will introduce new processes designed to provide greater transparency and assurance that users are paying no more than necessary for CS services.</p>
<p>The consultation paper seeks feedback on the key elements of the pricing policy, including:</p>
<ul><li>how and when ASX should take action to reimburse customers for any excess revenue or recover any revenue shortfalls;</li><li>how and when ASX should take action to review the CS services fee schedules; and</li><li>the proposed commencement date of the new Policy.</li></ul>
<p>ASX requests that responses are provided via the <a href="https://asx.au1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_1QVJO36uxxoUuFw" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">electronic form</a> by 25 October 2024. If the electronic form is unable to be used, please contact <a href="mailto:EquityPostTrade&#64;asx.com.au" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">EquityPostTrade&#64;asx.com.au</a>. </p>

<p>ASX thanks all stakeholders who took the time to provide a response.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>2/08/2024</td><td><p>On 2 August 2024, ASX published a consultation paper titled<u> </u><a href="/content/dam/asx/markets/clearing-and-settlement-services/chess-replacement-consultation-on-the-scope-and-implementation-of-chess-replacement-release-2.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Consultation on the scope and implementation of CHESS replacement Release 2 (settlement and subregister)</a>. The consultation paper outlines ASX&#39;s proposed plan for Release 2 of the CHESS replacement system, seeking feedback on design, scope, schedule, and transition for Release 2, a plan for timing and approach on a potential shift to T&#43;1 settlement cycle, as well as interoperability, testing and industry readiness approaches. </p>

<p>This consultation paper sought feedback on:</p>

<p>ASX thanks all stakeholders that provided written feedback. Given the overall support for a staged implementation, and for the proposed design, scope and schedule for Release 1 of the CHESS Replacement Project, ASX does not propose to make material changes to the Release 1 design and scope proposals as set out in the consultation paper.</p>
<p>Some adjustments have been made to the proposed industry testing timeframes for Release 1, which have resulted in corresponding changes to the proposed overall Release 1 timeline. The suite of Release 1 industry testing documentation has also been updated. </p>
<p>The Release 1 go-live date will be set with industry stakeholders as part of finalising the Release 1 Cutover and Migration Approach documentation, targeted for publication in Q2 2025.</p>
<p>ASX will continue to engage with stakeholder working groups that report to the CHESS Replacement Technical Committee on aspects of testing, cutover and go-live which may need to be further refined over time. </p>
</td></tr><tr><td>13/05/2024</td><td><p>On 13 May 2024, ASX released a consultation paper titled <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2024/consultation-paper-for-asx-clear-asx-settlement-and-austraclear.pdf">ASX clearing and settlement operating rules review and refresh</a>.</p>
<p>This consultation paper outlines proposed amendments that relate to the five year review and refresh of the ASX Clear Operating Rules and Procedures, ASX Settlement Operating Rules and Procedures and Austraclear Regulations and Procedures.</p>
<p>This includes enhancements to support continued compliance with clearing and settlement facility licence obligations such as a broader power to request information from participants, a requirement for clearing participants to notify and update contacts to support the use of recovery powers, and a broader emergency power to enable ASX Clear to take action if an undesirable situation or practice develops that is contrary to a fair and effective clearing and settlement facility or the reduction of systemic risk.</p>
<p>ASX welcomes feedback from stakeholders on the draft rule amendments. Written submissions are requested by 12 July 2024.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>13/05/2024</td><td><p>On 13 May 2024, ASX released a consultation paper titled <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2024/consultation-paper-for-asx-clear-futures-may-2024.pdf">ASX 24 and ASX Clear (Futures) – Change to position reporting framework and review and refresh of operating rules</a>.</p>
<p>This consultation paper outlines proposed amendments to the ASX 24 Operating Rules and Procedures and ASX Clear (Futures) Operating Rules and Procedures that relate to:</p>
<ul><li>the transfer of obligations for allocations, position limits and daily reporting of Open Positions from Trading Participants to Clearing Participants. The amendments also introduce additional fields for position reporting and clarify the requirements for managing net-down obligations (including post-expiry). To support the amendments, ASX Clear (Futures) proposes to introduce a Guidance Note on position management.   </li><li>the five year review and refresh of the ASX Clear (Futures) Operating Rules and Procedures. This includes enhancements to support continued compliance with clearing and settlement facility licence obligations such as a broader power to request information from participants, a requirement for clearing participants to notify and update contacts to support the use of recovery powers, and a broader emergency power to enable ASX Clear (Futures) to take action if an undesirable situation or practice develops that is contrary to a fair and effective clearing and settlement facility or the reduction of systemic risk.</li></ul>
<p>ASX welcomes feedback from stakeholders on the draft rule amendments. Written submissions are requested by 12 July 2024.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>23/04/2024</td><td><p>On 23 April 2024, ASX published an industry whitepaper following on from the establishment of the T&#43;1 working group. The ASX Business Committee formed the T&#43;1 Working Group in December 2023 to provide analysis and insights to the Business Committee on settlement cycle compression. Working group members have provided input into this paper. The paper <a href="/content/dam/asx/markets/clearing-and-settlement-services/t1-whitepaper-042024.pdf">Considerations for accelerating cash equities settlement in Australia to T&#43;1</a> explores strategic considerations for a potential transition to T&#43;1.</p>
<p>Stakeholders are encouraged to provide written feedback by 18 June 2024 via <a href="https://asx.au1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6RSO33Hz7ektVDU" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Qualtrics</a>. Feedback will be compiled and shared where appropriate. ASX will aim to publish a summary of feedback in August 2024.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>17/04/2024</td><td><p>On 17 April 2024, ASX released a consultation paper titled <a href="/content/dam/asx/markets/clearing-and-settlement-services/chess-replacement-partnership-program-consultation-paper-20240417.pdf">CHESS Replacement Partnership Program: Development Incentive Pool Future Milestones Consultation Paper</a>. </p>
<p>This consultation paper invites feedback on the proposed structure of the future payment milestones and allocation of funds under the CHESS Replacement Partnership Program (Partnership Program) Development Incentive Pool. The Partnership Program is designed to encourage continued participation in the CHESS replacement project by supporting eligible participants (Program Participants) to undertake the requisite technological and associated development activities to successfully interface with Release 2 of the CHESS replacement solution. The proposed milestones represent Release 2 critical path milestones that require uplift from eligible Program Participants to support increased engagement and testing activities. </p>
<p>ASX welcomes industry feedback on the proposals outlined in this consultation paper, which will be key in helping ASX to make an informed decision regarding a payment milestone structure and allocation of funds that benefits all relevant stakeholders. Written submissions are requested by 15 May 2024.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>14/03/2024</td><td><p>On 14 March 2024, ASX released a consultation paper titled <a href="/content/dam/asx/markets/clearing-and-settlement-services/chess-replacement-consultation-paper-on-staged-implementation-approach-andimplementation-of-release-1-clearing-services.pdf">Consultation Paper on Staged Implementation Approach and Implementation of Release 1 (Clearing Services)</a>.   </p>
<p>This consultation paper discusses the details of the proposed staged implementation of the CHESS replacement solution across two main releases, and seeks industry feedback on a high-level project plan and an indicative timeline for those releases, including their design, scope and timing. It also seeks input on the proposed scope of and implementation approach for Release 1, including system development and testing, technical accreditation, documentation and operational readiness. The proposed first release will implement the new solution for the clearing component of CHESS and Financial Information eXchange (FIX) messaging for trade registration for all market operators, and is designed to minimise disruption for Clearing and Settlement (CS) Participants by maintaining the existing CHESS message interface and business processes, and offering a familiar operational environment.</p>
<p>This is the first of two consultation papers seeking feedback on the staged implementation approach to CHESS replacement. Feedback received in response to this consultation paper will inform ASX’s second consultation targeted for Q3 2024 which will seek stakeholder feedback on the proposed Release 2, which will implement the remaining clearing components, settlement and subregister functionality and updated messaging interfaces to participants, registries and payment providers.  </p>
<p>ASX welcomes industry views on the proposals outlined in this consultation paper. In addition to seeking feedback, this consultation paper is intended to provide information to impacted stakeholders to enable them to commence planning and allocating their own resources to implement CHESS replacement. Written submissions are requested by 24 April 2024.  </p>
</td></tr></tbody></table>

        <div class="accordion__item__header beforeBorder" role="accordion" tabindex="0">
            <i class="asx-icon-up gtm-accordion"></i>
            <h6 class="gtm-accordion">2023</h6>
        </div>
        <div class="accordion__item__body hidden">

            


<div class="aem-Grid aem-Grid--12 aem-Grid--default--12 ">
    
    <div class="table-component aem-GridColumn aem-GridColumn--default--12">
 
  <div class="table-container  paddingbottom60 normalTable">
    
    <div data-table-fix-col="0" data-table-fix-row="0" class="rebrand-datatables  ''">
        
            <table border="0" width="100%" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="1"><thead></thead><tbody><tr style="	text-align: left;
"><td><b>Date</b></td><th width="90%"><b>Description</b></th></tr><tr><td>30/11/2023</td><td><p>On 30 November 2023 ASX release its <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/response-to-consultation-on-aqua-product-rule-amendments.pdf">Response to Consultation Feedback</a> regarding proposed Rule Amendments to facilitate the implementation of ASIC’s updated exchange traded product (ETP) naming expectations. <br />
</p>
<p>ASX received one non-confidential submission from the <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/financial-services-council-submission.pdf">Financial Services Council</a> (FSC) and no confidential submissions in response to the ASX Consultation Paper.  The FSC represents a range of stakeholders including product issuers, investment managers and financial advisers. ASX thanks the FSC for providing its submission.</p>
<p>The response to consultation feedback contains a summary of stakeholder feedback received and ASX’s response to such feedback, including related updates to the draft rule amendments.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>27/11/2023</td><td><p>On 27 November 2023, ASX released a paper (<a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/response-to-consultation-on-the-future-of-the-asx-managed-fund-settlement-service.pdf">Response to consultation on the future of the ASX Managed Fund Settlement Service</a>) summarising responses received to the 6 July 2023 consultation paper entitled <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/asx-managed-fund-settlement-service-consultation-paper.pdf">Consultation on the future of the ASX Managed Fund Settlement Service</a>. </p>
<p>The consultation paper sought stakeholder feedback in two key areas:</p>
<ul><li>Industry preferences for dealing in managed funds via ASX; and</li><li>A proposed process for winding down and closing mFund, if appropriate.</li></ul>
<p>ASX received 18 written responses from stakeholders including 11 responsible entities/product issuers, 4 Trading/Settlement Participants, a Product Issuer Settlement Participant/Unit Registry, and 2 industry associations. </p>
<p>Public non-confidential submissions were received from the following respondents:</p>
<ul><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/fsc-submission-to-asx-consultation-on-the-future-of-asx-managed-fund-settlement-service.pdf">FSC Submission</a></li><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/acsa-response-to-asx-consultation-paper.pdf">ACSA Submission</a></li></ul>
<p>ASX would like to thank the stakeholders that provided written feedback. This feedback has helped inform ASX’s assessment of the future value that mFund can provide to the Australian market. Based on this assessment, ASX has determined to wind down and close the mFund service with a target removal date for funds by 31 May 2026, a period of approximately two years and six months. Further detail regarding the matters taken into account by ASX are set out in the Response paper.  </p>
<p>ASX is committed to providing an orderly wind down of the mFund service and will establish an industry working group with stakeholders to facilitate communication during the wind down period and assist with the scheduling of closure activities.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>13/09/23</td><td><p>On 13 September 2023, ASX released a paper (<a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/summary-of-responses-enhancing-the-asx-investment-products-offering.pdf">Summary of Responses - Enhancing the ASX Investment Products Offering</a>) summarising responses received to the 26 April 2022 consultation paper entitled <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/investment-products-phase-1-consultation-paper-final.pdf?_gl&#61;1*k5ppe3*_ga*NzU1NjcyNDU5LjE2NDYxMDEwODc.*_ga_J1L799T374*MTY5Mzk4NzE2NS4yNTYuMS4xNjkzOTg3NjIyLjUzLjAuMA..">Enhancing the ASX Investment Products Offering</a>. </p>
<p>The consultation paper was broad-ranging, seeking submissions from all interested stakeholders on a range of policy issues, including:</p>
<ul><li>admission requirements and processes</li><li>product names</li><li>investment mandates</li><li>permitted investments</li><li>portfolio disclosure</li><li>management agreements</li><li>management fees and costs</li><li>performance reporting</li><li>liquidity support</li><li>the mFund Settlement Service, and</li><li>improving the information available to investors about investment products.</li></ul>
<p>This response paper summarises the consultation feedback received by ASX. It does not propose any new policy positions. Given the volume and range of feedback provided, ASX will be considering and prioritising which aspects of the consultation it will seek to progress before releasing a second phase consultation. ASX will update stakeholders accordingly as we progress our analysis.<b><u></u></b></p>
<p><b>Consultation feedback</b></p>

<p>Public non-confidential submissions were received from the following respondents:</p>
<ul><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/alternative-investment-management-association.pdf">Alternative Investment Management Association</a></li><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/australian-custodial-services-association.pdf">Australian Custodial Services Association</a></li><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/bell-potter-securities.pdf">Bell Potter Securities</a></li><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/blue-tractor-group.pdf">Blue Tractor Group</a></li><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/financial-services-council.pdf">Financial Services Council</a></li><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/listed-investment-company-and-trust-association.pdf">Listed Investment Company &amp; Trust Association</a></li><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/morningstar.pdf">Morningstar</a></li><li><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/the-australian-financial-markets-association.pdf">The Australian Financial Markets Association</a></li></ul>
<p><b>Relationship with other consultations</b></p>

<p>This response to consultation summarises the feedback received to the matters raised in the 26 April 2022 Consultation Paper only.  ASX will engage with the feedback provided in relation to other consultations listed above as set out in their respective consultation materials.</p>
<p><b>Further information</b></p>
<p>For more information, please reach out to Andrew Campion, GM, Investment Products &amp; Strategy: <a href="mailto:Andrew.Campion&#64;asx.com.au">Andrew.Campion&#64;asx.com.au</a></p>

</td></tr><tr><td valign="top">07/06/23</td><td><p>On 7 June 2023, ASX released a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/consultation-paper-aqua-rule-amendments-info-230-naming-conventions.pdf">consultation paper</a> on amendments to the ASX Operating Rules and ASX Settlement Operating Rules to facilitate the implementation of ASIC’s updated exchange traded product (ETP) naming expectations set out in the revised version of INFO 230 released by ASIC in November 2022. </p>
<p>This includes amendments to align categories of AQUA products that may be admitted to trading status with ASIC’s updated ETP naming conventions - which no longer contemplate a Managed Fund as an ETP product label (with the only primary labels contemplated for ETPs being Exchange Traded Fund (or ETF) or Structured Product (or Structured)), as well as a number of other structural drafting improvements and tidy-up changes to the AQUA Rules which it is opportune to make at this time.</p>
<p>The consultation paper invites feedback from stakeholders on the operation of the draft rule amendments, including any unintended consequences and associated impacts. The consultation paper also identifies some specific amendments in relation to which feedback is sought.</p>
<p>Written submissions are requested by 19 July 2023.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>23/05/23</td><td><p>On 23 May 2023, ASX released a response paper (<a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/response-to-consultation-paper-3-on-asx-testing-uplift-environments-and-bcp.pdf">Consultation 3 Response</a>) summarising and responding to the feedback from the 28 February 2023 Consultation 3 on ASX Market Management – Testing Uplift, Environments and BCP (<a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/market-management-consultation-3-asx-testing-uplift-environments-and-bcp.pdf">Consultation 3</a>)</p>
<p>The Consultation 3 Response includes the proposed actions ASX will take following the comprehensive program of stakeholder engagement ASX has undertaken since the release of Consultation 3.</p>
<p>Consultation 3 was the final of three ASX consultations in response to the Australian Securities and Investments Commission’s (ASIC) Report 708 - ‘ASIC’s expectation for industry in responding to a market outage’.</p>
<p>Consultation 3 sought stakeholder feedback across the following five topics:</p>
<ul><li>Enhancements to ASX Platform Test Strategy</li><li>Simulation Testing with Market Participants</li><li>Market Operators’ Interconnectedness</li><li>Improvements to BCP Strategy</li><li>Customer Test Environments.</li></ul>
<p>ASX received 14 written responses from a broad range of stakeholders including Participants (9), industry bodies (2), vendors (2), and a market operator (1).</p>
<p>Following the feedback and analysis of the Consultation 3 responses, ASX will now propose to:<br />
</p>
<ul><li>Increase the number of BCP events to two per year.</li><li>Incorporate new scenarios into BCP testing including an ALC Customer Network failure and CANCEL_ONLY session state functionality.</li><li>Develop an improved capability to simulate ‘production-like’ transaction profiles during BCP and IWT events.</li><li>Communicate more prescriptive test plans for BCP and IWT events including expectations on customers.</li><li>Continue to collaborate with AMOs on industry testing including scenarios and alignment of dates to minimise risks and impacts on costs and resourcing.</li><li>Investigate simulating large trading days in the Customer Development Environments (CDE).</li><li>Extend hours of availability for Exchange Traded Options in the CDE.</li><li>Investigate provisioning of a Signal B feed in the CDE (currently available in CDE&#43; only).</li></ul>
<p>ASX will now move to the planning and development stage for these proposals and will update stakeholders accordingly. For more information, please reach out to the ASX contacts listed in the consultation or via your Technical Account Managers.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td valign="top">28/02/23</td><td><p>On 28 February 2023, ASX released <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/market-management-consultation-3-asx-testing-uplift-environments-and-bcp.pdf">Market Management Consultation 3: ASX Testing Uplift, Environments and BCP</a> which is the third in a sequence of three consultations that the ASX has undertaken following ASIC’s expectations of market operators set out in ASIC’s Report 708.</p>
<p>The first consultation in June 2022 primarily focused on existing procedures and current capabilities during incident management. The second consultation in October 2022 outlined and provided technical details for future enhancements to these procedures and capabilities.</p>
<p>In this third market consultation, ASX is providing information and seeking stakeholder feedback across the following topics:</p>
<ul><li>Enhancements to ASX Platform Test Strategy</li><li>Simulation Testing with Market Participants</li><li>Market Operators’ Interconnectedness</li><li>Improvements to BCP Strategy</li><li>Customer Test Environments.</li></ul>
<p>Written submissions should be made by 14 April 2023.<br />
</p>
</td></tr><tr><td valign="top">31/01/23</td><td><p>On 31 January 2023, ASX released a response paper (<a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/response-to-consultation-paper-2-asx-market-management-potential-enhancements.pdf">Consultation 2 Response</a>) summarising and responding to the feedback from the 31 October 2022 Consultation 2 on ASX Market Management and potential enhancements (<a href="https://www2.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/ASX-market-management-consultation-2-potential-enhancements.pdf">Consultation 2</a>).  The Consultation 2 Response includes the proposed actions ASX will take following the comprehensive program of stakeholder engagement which ASX has undertaken following the release of Consultation 2.</p>
<p>Consultation 2 was the second of three ASX consultations in response to the Australian Securities and Investments Commission’s (ASIC) Report 708 - ‘ASIC’s expectation for industry in responding to a market outage’.</p>
<p>Consultation 2 sought stakeholder feedback across the following four proposals:</p>
<ul><li>A new order download service (ODS).</li><li>A new trade download service (TDS).</li><li>A ‘cancel only’ session state.</li><li>An intraday reboot capability of the ASX Trade system.</li></ul>
<p>ASX received 15 written responses from a broad range of stakeholders including participants (9), industry bodies (3), vendors (2) and a market operator (1).</p>
<p>Following the feedback and analysis of the Consultation 2 responses, ASX is now proposing to introduce the automated Order and Trade Download Services and a ‘Cancel Only’ Session State. ASX will now move to the planning and development stage for this functionality and will update stakeholders accordingly. </p>
<p>ASX will not progress with the development of an intraday reboot capability (turning off and restarting ASX Trade) as the majority of stakeholders were generally unsupportive of introducing this functionality due to the complexity and significant development work required.</p>

            <table border="0" cellpadding="1" cellspacing="0" width="100%"><tbody><tr><td width="10%"><b>Date</b></td><th>Description</th></tr><tr><td valign="top">31/10/22</td><td><p>Today’s publication of the <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/ASX-market-management-consultation-2-potential-enhancements.pdf">“ASX Market Management Consultation 2: Potential Enhancements”</a> is the second in a sequence of three consultations that the ASX will be undertaking following ASIC’s expectations of market operators set out in ASIC’s Report 708.</p>
<p>Following the feedback received during the first consultation, which primarily focussed upon existing procedures and current capabilities during incidents, this second consultation will outline and provide technical details for potential future enhancements to these procedures and capabilities. <br />
</p>
<p>The ASX is seeking stakeholder feedback across the following four proposals:<br />
</p>
<ul><li>A new order download service (ODS).</li><li>A new trade download service (TDS).</li><li>A ‘cancel only’ session state.</li><li>An Intraday restart capability.</li></ul>
<p>The final section of this second consultation will detail ASX’s policies for disabling certain market components, as set out by ASIC’s Rep 708 Expectation 6. Note: ASX is not seeking feedback on this section, and it is tabled in this document as a technical reference only.<br />
</p>
<p>As part of ASX’s ongoing commitment to work with all stakeholders during this consultation, we will again, conduct a range of group and one-on-one meetings over the next six weeks.<br />
</p>

</p>

The paper includes the proposed actions ASX will take following the consultation.</p>
