</td></tr><tr><td valign="top">28/06/22</td><td><p>On 28 June 2022, ASX released a Consultation Paper on<b> </b><u><a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/market-management-consultation-28062022.pdf">Market Management</a>.</u></p>
<p>This consultation paper follows a review of actions taken by the ASX during technical issues or outages.   The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) published ASIC’s expectations for industry in responding to a market outage (Report 708).  The report sets out ASIC’s ‘expectations to support the resilience and robustness of the Australian equity market’ that are applicable to market operators, market participants, and large institutional investors.</p>
<p>ASX is committed to working closely with our regulators, technology providers, independent experts, industry associations and customers to strengthen the resiliency and robustness of all the markets we operate, and to address the expectations listed in ASIC’s report about the equity market specifically.</p>
<p>A key part of this commitment is a sequence of three market consultations on aspects of ASX’s management of the equity market.  These are expected to be conducted in June, September and December 2022.</p>
<ul><li><b>June 2022 (this consultation</b>): Broadly assesses the current position and considers refinements and improvements based on current capabilities.</li><li><b>September 2022:</b> Will request stakeholder input on potential future capabilities.</li><li><b>December 2022:</b> Will request stakeholder feedback on participant testing needs, including changes arising from the first and second consultations.</li></ul>
<p>This first market consultation (June 2022) provides transparency on ASX’s existing market management procedures and how they are applied, and invites feedback on current practices based on the following four areas:</p>
<ol><li>Certainty about orders and trades during an outage</li><li>Market session states (including Enquire and Adjust modes)</li><li>Approach, frequency and content of communications</li><li>Intraday checkpoints and cut-off times.</li></ol>
<p>Written submissions should be made by 23 July 2022.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td valign="top">08/06/22</td><td><p>On 8th June 2022, ASX released a <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/consultation-paper-short-term-interest-rate-futures-fallback-provisions-june-2022.pdf">consultation paper</a> on the fallback language to be applied to the Australian and New Zealand 90 Day Bank Bill Futures in the event of permanent cessation of the 3 month BBSW and/or BKBM benchmark. The consultation requests feedback on:</p>
<ul><li>Proposed fallback language to be included in the ASX 24 Operating Rules and Procedures; and</li><li>Alternative fallback rates currently available and the level of detail participants require regarding the fallback rate and calculation ahead of any permanent cessation event.</li></ul>
<p>The proposed changes are in line with global benchmark reform and best practice guidance issued by regulators worldwide to include fallback language in all contractual arrangements.</p>
<p>Written submissions in response to the consultation paper are requested by Wednesday 6th July 2022.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td valign="top">01/06/22</td><td><p>On 1 June 2022, ASX released its response to submissions received on the March 2022 <a href="https://www2.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/issuers/issuer-services/issuer-services-discussion-paper-new-pricing.pdf">Discussion Paper - Issuer Services: New Pricing</a>. The changes proposed in the paper were relevant to any issuer of approved financial products that uses or will use ASX Issuer Services.</p>
<p>The <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/issuers/issuer-services/issuer-services-response-to-submissions-new-pricing-model.pdf">response</a> summarises the key themes from the consultation process and ASX’s reply. The paper also sets out the confirmed changes and effective date of 1 July 2022.</p>
<p>ASX received 9 submissions in response to the Discussion Paper, with 3 provided on a confidential basis. The submissions provided on a non-confidential basis are available at the links below:</p>
<ul><li><a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/afma-submission.pdf">AFMA</a></li><li><a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/aira-submission.pdf">AIRA</a></li><li><a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/computershare-submission.pdf">Computershare</a></li><li><a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/gia-submission.pdf">GIA</a></li><li><a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/nsx-submission.pdf">NSX</a></li><li><a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/stephen-dear-submission.pdf">Stephen Dear</a></li></ul>
</td></tr><tr><td valign="top">26/04/22</td><td valign="top"><p>On 26 April 2022, ASX released a consultation paper entitled <a href="https://www2.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/investment-products-phase-1-consultation-paper-final.pdf">Enhancing the ASX Investment Products Offering</a>.</p>
<p>The consultation paper is phase one of a two-stage consultation process intended to ensure that ASX’s investment product offering is supported by a clear and consistent rule framework that safeguards the interests of investors, while at the same time providing issuers with the flexibility to innovate and bring new products to market, and without imposing undue compliance costs or burdens.</p>
<p>ASX’s investment product offering currently comprises the following product sets regulated by three different rule books:</p>
<ul><li>exchange traded funds (ETFs), managed funds and structured products quoted on ASX under schedule 10A of the ASX Operating Rules</li><li>listed investment companies (LICs), listed investment trusts (LITs), real estate investment trusts (REITs) and infrastructure funds listed and quoted on ASX under the ASX Listing Rules, and</li><li>warrants quoted on ASX under schedule 10 of the ASX Operating Rules.</li></ul>
<p>ASX can see merit in bringing these different rules into closer alignment for the benefit of both investors and issuers.</p>
<p>The consultation paper seeks submissions from all interested stakeholders on a range of policy issues relevant to achieving this outcome, including:</p>
<ul><li>admission requirements and processes</li><li>product names</li><li>investment mandates</li><li>permitted investments</li><li>portfolio disclosure</li><li>management agreements</li><li>management fees and costs</li><li>performance reporting</li><li>liquidity support</li><li>the mFund Settlement Service, and</li><li>improving the information available to investors about investment products.</li></ul>
<p>To assist stakeholders in making a submission, ASX has prepared a separate <a target="_blank" href="https://www2.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/response-form-asx-investment-products-phase-1-consultation-paper.docx" rel="noopener noreferrer">submission form</a> listing all of the questions in the consultation paper and providing a space for responses to those questions.</p>
<p>After considering the submissions it receives on the policy issues raised in the phase one consultation paper, ASX will proceed to draft proposed changes to its rules, procedures and guidance for investment products.</p>
<p>Phase two of the consultation will then seek feedback on the specific changes proposed to ASX’s rules, procedures and guidance for investment products. The consultation paper for phase two is likely to issue in early 2023.</p>
<p>Subject to the receipt of the necessary regulatory approvals, it is envisaged that the final changes to ASX’s rules, procedures and guidance for investment products will be released in mid-late 2023, with a view to them coming into effect no earlier than 1 January 2024.</p>
<p>Stakeholders who wish to make a submission on the phase one consultation paper are asked to do so in writing by the close of business on Friday 24 June 2022.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td valign="top">05/04/22</td><td><p>On 5 April 2022, ASX released a consultation paper entitled <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/omnibus-lr-consultation-paper-exposure-draft-amendments.pdf" title="Proposed enhancements to the ASX Listing Rules: Continually improving the reputation and integrity of the ASX market">Proposed enhancements to the ASX Listing Rules: Continually improving the reputation and integrity of the ASX market</a>.</p>
<p>The consultation paper seeks feedback from stakeholders on proposed enhancements to the ASX Listing Rules dealing with:</p>
<ul><li>the issuance of securities by listed entities, including the rules relating to security purchase plans (SPPs), pro rata issues and material placements</li><li>the financial reporting framework for listed entities</li><li> the admission of an entity to the official list and the quotation of its securities</li><li> transactions by listed entities with persons in a position of influence</li><li>the lodgement of documents by listed entities with ASX for release to the market, and</li><li>other miscellaneous matters.</li></ul>
<p>Stakeholders interested in making a submission on the consultation paper are asked to do so in writing by the close of business on Friday 27 May 2022.</p>
<p>ASX will consider all submissions it receives in response to the consultation paper before finalising the proposed rule amendments with ASIC.</p>
<p>Subject to the receipt of the necessary regulatory approvals, it is envisaged that the final rule amendments will be released in the third quarter of 2022 and take effect on 1 December 2022.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td valign="top">21/03/22</td><td><p>On 21 March 2022,  ASX released a <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/asx-consultation-otc-fallback-rates-and-otc-product-enhancements.pdf" title="enhancements">consultation paper</a> outlining <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/asx-consultation-otc-rules-and-handbook-changes-for-fallback-rates-and-otc-product-enhancements.pdf" title="proposed changes">proposed changes to the ASX Clear (Futures) OTC Rules and Handbook</a> to:</p>
<ul><li>implement benchmark fallback rate provisions in relation to the OTC interest rate derivatives products cleared by ASX; and</li><li>introduce OTC product enhancements to support the Actual/Actual ICMA Day Count Convention for the clearing of Assets Swaps and the IMM AUD roll convention, the industry convention to enable swaps to roll on ASX’s bank bill futures dates.  </li></ul>
<p>Written submissions are requested by Friday 29 April 2022.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td valign="top">03/03/22</td><td><p>On 3 March 2022, ASX released the <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/issuers/issuer-services/issuer-services-discussion-paper-new-pricing.pdf">Discussion Paper Issuer Services: New Pricing</a>. The changes proposed in the paper are relevant to any issuer of approved financial products that uses or will use ASX’s Issuer Services. The changes do not relate to listing fees.</p>
<p>ASX welcomes feedback from issuers on the pricing changes outlined in the paper.</p>
<p>Written submissions are requested by <b>Thursday 14 April 2022</b>.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td valign="top">11/02/22</td><td valign="top"><p>On 11 February 2022, ASX released a <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/recovery-rules-consultation-paper-11.02.2022.pdf" title="recovery rules consultation paper">consultation paper</a> outlining proposed changes to the ASX Recovery Rules and Handbook that relate to the allocation of US settlement bank investment losses between the ASX CCPs and their clearing participants</p>
<p>ASX seeks feedback from clearing participants in relation to ASX’s proposal to allocate USD settlement bank investment losses in excess of $75m between ASX Clear (Futures) ( <b>ASXCLF</b>) clearing participants based on principles of mutualisation and potential and actual user pays. While all ASXCLF clearing participants will be exposed to a US settlement bank loss, those clearing participants that are in scope for overnight margining, and those clearing participants who have also paid USD funds to ASXCLF in the prior default fund commitment period will each bear a greater proportion of any loss.</p>
<p>Written submissions in response to the consultation paper are requested by Friday 25 March 2022.<br />
</p>
</td></tr><tr><td valign="top">01/02/22</td><td valign="top"><p>On 1 February 2022, ASX Limited (“ASX”) released a consultation paper entitled <a title="proposal" href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/cciv-consultation-paper-final.pdf"><i>Proposed ASX rule amendments to facilitate the listing of CCIVs and certain other collective investment vehicles on the ASX market and the quotation of their products on the ASX AQUA market</i></a>.</p>
<p>The consultation paper seeks feedback on changes ASX is proposing to:</p>
<ul><li>the ASX Listing Rules to facilitate the listing on the ASX market of:<ul><li>CCIV sub-funds</li><li>notified foreign passport funds (“NFPFs”) and</li><li>NZ registered managed investment schemes making a recognised offer of securities under Chapter 8 of the Corporations Act (“recognised NZ schemes”), and</li></ul>
</li><li>the ASX Operating Rules to facilitate the admission of products issued by the entities listed above to trading status on the ASX Quoted Assets (“AQUA”) market or for settlement through the ASX Managed Funds Settlement Service (“mFund”).</li></ul>
<p>By way of background, a CCIV (short for “Corporate Collective Investment Vehicle”) is a new type of funds management vehicle to be introduced by the <i>Corporate Collective Investment Vehicle Framework and Other Measures Bill 2021</i> that will operate via one or more sub-funds. The target date for the implementation of that Bill is currently 1 July 2022. ASX wants to be able to offer CCIV sub-funds access to the distribution available on the ASX and AQUA market platforms and to offer investors access via the ASX and AQUA markets to the investment opportunities that CCIV sub-funds will provide. To do this requires changes to the ASX Listing Rules and the ASX Operating Rules.</p>
<p>As further background, NFPFs have the benefit of the Asia Region Funds Passport mutual recognition arrangements set out in Chapter 8A of the Corporations Act and explained further in ASIC Regulatory Guide 138 <i>Foreign Passport Funds</i>. Recognised NZ schemes have the benefit of the mutual recognition arrangements set out in Chapter 8 of the Corporations Act and explained further in <a href="https://download.asic.gov.au/media/5702539/rg190-published-25-july-2017-20200727.pdf">ASIC Regulatory Guide 190 <i>Offering financial products in New Zealand and Australia under mutual recognition</i></a>. Currently, however, ASX’s rules do not specifically cater for the listing of NFPFs or recognised NZ schemes or for the admission of their products as AQUA products, a situation which ASX is also seeking to rectify via this consultation.</p>
<p>ASX’s proposed rule changes will therefore be of particular interest to entities in the funds management industry and to industry groups and advisers representing those entities.</p>
<p>Due to the structure of CCIVs and their sub-funds, however, some significant rationalisation is required to the Listing Rules that refer to, or draw a distinction between, listed companies and listed trusts so that they appropriately apply where the listed entity is a CCIV sub-fund, which has no legal personality and is neither a company nor a trust. These broader changes to the Listing Rules will be of interest to all listed entities and their advisers.</p>
<p>Stakeholders interested in making a submission on the consultation paper are asked to do so in writing by the close of business on Friday 18 March 2022.</p>
<p>ASX will consider all submissions it receives in response to this consultation before finalising the proposed rule amendments.</p>
<p>Subject to the receipt of the necessary regulatory approvals, ASX is aiming to have the amended rules in force on, or as soon as practicable after, 1 July 2022, the Government’s target date for the introduction of its CCIV legislation.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td valign="top">17/01/2022</td><td><p>On 17 January 2022, ASX released its <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/asx-clear-response-paper-to-consultation-on-changes-to-capital-requirements.pdf" title="response to consultation">response to consultation</a> on the October 2020 <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2020/201014-consultation-paper-and-appendices.pdf" title="proposal">proposed changes to capital requirements for ASX Clear Participants</a>. The response to consultation paper includes an outline of the draft rule amendments to give effect to the recalibrated proposal.</p>
<p>ASX received seven written submissions in response to its consultation paper, with six provided on a confidential basis. The submission provided on a non-confidential basis is available at the link below:</p>
<ul><li><a></a><a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/201130-response-from-afma.pdf" title="AFMA response">AFMA</a></li></ul>
</td></tr></tbody></table>

</td></tr><tr><td valign="top">22/10/21</td><td><p>On 22 October 2021, ASX released its <a href="https://www2.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2021/listing-rules-chapter-5-consolidated-consultation-response.pdf">response</a> to the submissions it received on its consultation paper dated 16 April 2021 entitled <i><a target="_blank" href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2021/chapter-5-consultation-paper.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">Proposed changes to the oil and gas reporting requirements in the ASX Listing Rules</a></i>.</p>

</td></tr><tr><td valign="top">16/04/21</td><td><p>On 16 April 2021, ASX released a consultation paper entitled <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2021/chapter-5-consultation-paper.pdf">Proposed changes to the oil and gas reporting requirements in the ASX Listing Rules</a>.</p>

</td></tr><tr><td valign="top">24/03/21</td><td><p>On 24 March 2021, ASX Limited (“ASX”) released a detailed <a href="https://www2.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/documents/unlinked-docs/compliance/final-consultation-response-online-forms-notification-of-security-issues-and-corporate-action-timetables.pdf">Consultation Response</a> to its 30 November 2020 consultation paper <a href="https://www2.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2020/2020-stp-consultation-paper.pdf">Proposed Listing Rules changes: online forms, notification of security issues and corporate action timetables</a>.</p>
<p>The <a href="https://www2.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/documents/unlinked-docs/compliance/final-consultation-response-online-forms-notification-of-security-issues-and-corporate-action-timetables.pdf">Consultation Response</a> outlines a number of amendments to the Listing Rules (“LR”) that will come into effect on 5 June 2021 (or such later date as ASX may notify). The amendments include:</p>
<ul><li>changes to the timetables for seeking the quotation of securities in LR 2.8;</li><li>changes to the buy-back notification requirements in LR 3.8A;</li><li>changes to the notification requirements for issues, conversions and cancellations of securities, and for payment of calls, instalments and other amounts on partly paid securities, in LR 3.10.3 – 3.10.3E;</li><li>changes to LR 3.21 and 3.22 imposing some additional notification requirements around the cancellation, deferral or reduction of previously announced dividends, distributions or interest payments;</li><li>clarificatory changes to the definition of “employee incentive plan” in LR 19.12; and</li><li>changes to the timetables for corporate actions in Appendices 6A and 7A, in particular to allow an additional 2 business days for an entity to announce the results of certain corporate actions.</li></ul>
<p>The <a href="https://www2.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/documents/unlinked-docs/compliance/final-consultation-response-online-forms-notification-of-security-issues-and-corporate-action-timetables.pdf">Consultation Response</a> is accompanied by the following annexures:</p>
<p>A.      the <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/documents/unlinked-docs/compliance/annexure-a-final-listing-rule-amendments.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">final changes ASX is making to the Listing Rules</a> addressing the feedback received in consultation submissions;</p>
<p>B.      a <a href="https://www2.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/documents/unlinked-docs/compliance/annexure-b-compare-final-rules-to-consultation-rules.pdf">mark-up comparing the final rule changes to the consultation version</a>;</p>
<p>and the final versions of the following new or amended Listing Rule Appendices:</p>
<p>C.      <a href="https://www2.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/documents/unlinked-docs/compliance/annexure-c-appendix-2a.pdf">Appendix 2A Application for quotation of securities</a>;</p>
<p>D.      <a href="https://www2.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/documents/unlinked-docs/compliance/annexure-d-appendix-3a.1.pdf">Appendix 3A.1 Notification of dividend/distribution</a>;</p>
<p>E.      <a href="https://www2.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/documents/unlinked-docs/compliance/annexure-e-appendix-3a.2.pdf">Appendix 3A.2 Notification of interest payment &amp; interest rate change</a>;</p>
<p>F.      <a href="https://www2.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/documents/unlinked-docs/compliance/annexure-f-appendix-3a.5.pdf">Appendix 3A.5 Notification of return of capital by way of in specie distribution of securities in another entity</a>;</p>
<p>G.      <a href="https://www2.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/documents/unlinked-docs/compliance/annexure-g-appendix-3a.6.pdf">Appendix 3A.6 Notification of call/instalment on quoted partly paid equity securities</a>;</p>
<p>H.      <a href="https://www2.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/documents/unlinked-docs/compliance/annexure-h-appendix-3b.pdf">Appendix 3B Announcement of proposed issue of securities</a>;</p>
<p>I.        <a href="https://www2.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/documents/unlinked-docs/compliance/annexure-i-appendix-3c.pdf">Appendix 3C Notification of buy-back</a>;</p>
<p>J.       <a href="https://www2.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/documents/unlinked-docs/compliance/annexure-j-appendix-3g.pdf">Appendix 3G Notification of issue, conversion or payment up of unquoted equity securities</a>; and</p>
<p>K.      <a href="https://www2.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/documents/unlinked-docs/compliance/annexure-k-appendix-3h.pdf">Appendix 3H Notification of cessation of securities</a>.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td valign="top">26/02/21</td><td><p>On 26 February 2021, ASX released a <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2021/20210226-asx-review-of-legal-terms-for-theasx-trade-acceptance-service-and-related-product-services.pdf">Review</a> of Legal Terms for the ASX Trade Acceptance Service and related Product Services (referred to collectively as the TAS). </p>
<p>The Legal Terms commenced on 31 October 2016, with a term of five years - due to expire on 31 October 2021. The Legal Terms provide that a review be commenced 12 months prior to the expiry of the Legal Terms and that the review be published within four months of its commencement.</p>
<p>The Review has not identified a need for significant changes to the Legal Terms. Accordingly the TAS will continue to be made available on substantially the same terms for another five years, with effect from 31 October 2021. The proposed changes to the Legal Terms identified through the Review are explained in the Review paper. Attachments A and B to the Review paper set out in mark-up the proposed changes to the Legal Terms.</p>
<p>The Legal Terms will also be reviewed and updated in conjunction with the replacement of the existing CHESS system prior to the expiry of that term</p>
</td></tr><tr><td valign="top">18/02/21</td><td><p>On 18 February 2021, ASX released its consultation paper on <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/participants/clearing-and-settlement/chess-replacement/stakeholder-communications/asx-chess-replacement-project-consultation-paper-proposed-changes-to-netting-and-settlement-workflow.pdf">CHESS Replacement: Proposed changes to netting and settlement workflow</a>. The consultation paper outlines proposed changes to the design of both the netting and settlement confirmation workflows to deliver processing efficiencies and reduce subsequent messaging volumes as part of the overnight end-of-day process and daily batch settlement.</p>
<p>The proposed changes will allow the CHESS replacement system to support clearing and settlement of significantly greater trading volumes and are largely in response to the extreme record trading activity in March 2020, which redefined the Day 1 capacity requirements of the replacement system. </p>
<p>The consultation period closed on 18 March 2021.</p>
</td></tr></tbody></table>

<ul><li>changes to the rules dealing with notifications of security issues in Listing Rules 3.10.3 – 3.10.3D to make them clearer and easier to follow;</li><li>amendments to Listing Rules 3.21 and 3.22 and a new Listing Rule 12.13 addressing the cancellation or deferral of previously announced dividends, distributions and interest payments;</li><li>an amendment to Listing Rule 2.8.3 to reduce the deadline for applying for quotation of securities issued as a consequence of the conversion of unquoted convertible securities from 10 business days to 5 business days;</li><li>clarificatory amendments to the definition of “employee incentive plan” in Listing Rule 19.12; and</li><li>changes to the timetables for corporate actions in Appendices 6A and 7A, in particular to allow an additional 2 business days for an entity to announce the results of certain corporate actions.</li></ul>

This response provides a summary of the feedback received, the key factors driving the project extension and the confirmed implementation schedule for CHESS replacement.</p>
<p>ASX received feedback from 100 organisations who responded to the consultation. The replanning process involved detailed discussions with our technology partners, the completion of a comprehensive project review and engagement with the regulatory agencies.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>14/10/20</td><td><p>On 14 October 2020, ASX released a <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2020/201014-consultation-paper-and-appendices.pdf">consultation paper</a> which outlines a proposed consolidation of the two capital measures that non-bank ASX Clear participants are currently required to maintain as per Schedule 1 of the ASX Clear Operating Rules, into a single capital measure. </p>
<p>ASX seeks feedback on the proposed single capital measure, as well as on draft miscellaneous rule amendments which has been included to ensure currency and accuracy of references.</p>
<p>Written submissions are requested by Monday, 30 November 2020.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>30/09/20</td><td>On 30 September 2020, ASX released a <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2020/final-consultation-paper-including-attachments-a-and-b.PDF">consultation paper</a> outlining proposed changes to the ASX Clear (Futures) Operating Rules and Procedures that relate to the default management of exchange traded derivatives (“ETDs”).   <br />
<br />
ASX seeks feedback from clearing participants and end-user clients of ETDs in relation to ASX’s proposal to introduce a clear and transparent framework for the auctioning of ETDs by ASX Clear (Futures) (“ASXCLF”) in the event that a futures clearing participant defaults.   <br />
<br />
ASX also seeks feedback from clearing participants in relation to ASX’s proposal to align default management powers available to both ASX Clear and ASXCLF through the extension of the existing ASXCLF indemnity.   <br />
<br />
Written submissions in response to the consultation paper are requested by Friday 13 November 2020.   <br />
 </td></tr><tr><td>24/09/20</td><td><p>On 24 September 2020, ASX released its <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2020/tranche2-response-to-cp-september2020-final-933157v1.pdf">response to consultation feedback</a> received on the February 2020 <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2020/tranche2-consultation-paper-and-attachments.PDF">CHESS Replacement Tranche 2 Rule Amendments Consultation Paper</a>.</p>

The market will be updated on the timing for the further rules consultation in ASX’s response to consultation feedback on the revised implementation timeline.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>27/07/2020</td><td><p>On the 27th of July 2020, ASX released its <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2020/bbsw-methodology-enhancements-consultation-paper.pdf">consultation paper on proposed changes to the BBSW methodology</a>. The objective of the changes are to increase the frequency with which BBSW rates are calculated using transaction data, while ensuring that a high quality rate is produced. The proposed enhancements relate solely to the transaction layer of the BBSW calculation waterfall.</p>
<p>ASX Benchmarks invites feedback from market participants and BBSW subscribers on the proposed methodology enhancements set out in this consultation paper. The consultation will be open from 27 July 2020 to 27 August 2020. Responses can be submitted to <a href="mailto:ASXBPricing&#64;asx.com.au">ASXBPricing&#64;asx.com.au</a>. </p>
<p>ASX Benchmarks will publish a market notice to advise market participants and BBSW subscribers of the outcome of the consultation in September 2020. ASX proposes to implement the methodology changes in November 2020, subject to the feedback received from this consultation paper.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>30/06/2020</td><td><p>On 30 June 2020, ASX released its consultation paper on the <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/markets/clearing-and-settlement-services/chess-replacement-consultation-paper-revised-implementation-timetable.pdf">CHESS Replacement Revised Implementation Timetable</a>. The paper sets out key project activities and milestones including system development and testing, user testing, technical accreditation, operational readiness, and operating rule amendments. The <a target="_blank" href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/media-releases/2020/asx-consultation-on-new-implementation-date-for-chess-replacement-media-release.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">media release</a> can be viewed online.</p>
<p>The revised timetable has been produced to provide additional time for the ongoing impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on all stakeholders, accommodate functionality changes requested by users, and have a longer period for ASX and CHESS users to complete their respective development and readiness activities. The aggregate effect of these considerations produces a new go-live date of April 2022, 12 months beyond the original target go-live.</p>
<p>While no-one was predicting this significant increase in trading volumes that have occurred recently, it highlights the need to replace older systems across the industry with flexible, contemporary technology. This requires prioritisation by ASX and CHESS users, but also prudent planning given the impact of COVID-19 to ensure that CHESS is replaced both in a safe and timely manner.</p>
<p>Written submissions from CHESS users are requested by 28 July 2020.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>22/05/2020</td><td><p>On 22 May 2020, ASX released its <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2020/tranche-1-response-to-cp-may-2020-full-910959v1.PDF">response to consultation feedback</a> received on the November 2019 <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/participants/clearing-and-settlement/chess-replacement/Chess-Replacement-Tranche1-Rule-Amendment.PDF" title="chess">CHESS Replacement Tranche 1 Rule Amendments Consultation Paper</a>.</p>

<p>ASX received 36 written submissions in response to the consultation paper, all of which were provided on a confidential basis.</p>
<p>ASX intends to implement a reduction to the 3 and 10 Year Bond Futures minimum price increment during the week of the Roll. These changes and the target implementation date are outlined in the response paper.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td width="10%"><p>21/02/2020</p>
</td><td width="90%"><p>On 21 February 2020, ASX released a <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2020/tranche2-consultation-paper-and-attachments.PDF">consultation paper</a> on the second of three tranches of operating rule amendments required to facilitate the implementation of the new system that will replace CHESS. These relate to corporate actions, mFund and RTGS payment aspects for &#39;Day 1&#34; implementation of CHESS Replacement system functionality. RTGS will support payments for corporate action involving entitlement acceptances as well as payments for bilateral demand settlement instructions (addressed in the tranche 1 rule amendments).</p>
<p>The consultation paper invites feedback from users and other stakeholders on the operation of the draft tranche 2 rule amendments, including any unintended consequences.</p>
<p>Written submissions are requested by Friday 3 April 2020.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td width="10%"><p>8/01/2020</p>
</td><td width="90%"><p>On 8 January 2020, ASX released a <a href="https://www.asx.com.au/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2020/asx-24-trade-cancellation-policy-consultation-paper.pdf">consultation paper</a> outlining proposed changes to the ASX 24 Trade Cancellation Policy, specifically, </p>
<ul><li>The removal of the No Cancellation Ranges (NCR) for all exchange traded options (ETOs), including the Single Session Options.</li><li>Amendment to the Extreme Trade Range (ETR) for the 20 Year Bond Futures product. </li><li>ASX is also seeking feedback on the current cancellation ranges for all other ASX 24 products. </li></ul>
<p>ASX proposes, subject to feedback received through consultation, to:</p>
<ul><li>Remove the NCR for ETOs to provide greater flexibility for market participants. This is in line with Trading Participant feedback and will further align the ASX 24 and ASX Trade Operating Rules Procedures. </li><li>Amend the ETR range of the 20 Year Treasury Bond Futures from 50 basis points to 25 basis points to reduce the likelihood of an error trade causing a negative impact on a participant. The reduced ETR price level will provide a balance between allowing a reasonable range where erroneous trades will be cancelled whilst not unnecessarily impacting trading activity on days with high levels of market volatility.</li><li>Assess whether the current cancellation ranges for all ASX 24 products are appropriate.</li></ul>
<p>Written submissions are requested by Friday 28th February 2020. </p>

      <div class="cmp-text ">
        <h3><a id="policy-submissions-to-government"></a>Policy submissions to government</h3>
<h4>2026</h4>

      </div>
    
    
    
    

  </div></div>


    
    
    <div class="table-component">
 
  <div class="table-container paddingtop15  normalTable">
    
    <div data-table-fix-col="0" data-table-fix-row="0" class="rebrand-datatables  ''">
        
            <table border="0" cellpadding="1" cellspacing="0" width="100%"><tbody><tr><td width="10%"><b>Date</b></td><td><b>Description</b></td><td> </td></tr><tr><td>25/09/2026</td><td colspan="2"><p>On 25 September 2026, ASX provided a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/strengthening-australias-legislative-response-to-modern-slavery-in-supply-chains.pdf">submission</a> to the consultation on Strengthening Australia’s Response to Modern Slavery in Supply Chains, which proposes a new corporate criminal offence for failing to prevent modern slavery in supply chains.</p>
<p>The ASX submission recommends that the Government first finalise the underlying enhanced modern slavery obligations before undertaking consultation to introduce a new criminal offence. It also recommends a phased approach that prioritises guidance, capability uplift and supervisory engagement to support effective implementation and strengthen modern slavery risk management prior to the introduction of a criminal offence.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>25/09/2026</td><td colspan="2"><p>On Friday 25 September 2026, ASX made a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/innovative-business-cgt-concession-exposure-draft-legislation.pdf">submission</a> to the Treasury consultation on exposure draft legislation for the proposed capital gains tax reforms for innovative start-ups. Further to ASX’s July submission, the submission responds to the exposure draft proposal of maintaining the concession for eligible unlisted companies only.</p>
<p>The submission reiterates ASX’s concern that the concession is limited to investments in unlisted companies, even where all other eligibility criteria is met. The policy should be designed to support investment in early-stage innovative companies regardless of whether capital is raised through public or private markets. ASX recommends the concession be extended to newly issued equity in an innovative company whether listed or unlisted, where all other eligibility requirements are met.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>09/07/26</td><td>On 9 July 2026, ASX made a <a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2026/asx-submission-capital-gains-tax-reforms-arrangements-for-innovative-start-ups.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">submission</a> to the Treasury consultation on the proposed capital gains tax reforms for innovative start-ups. ASX’s submission recommended extending the proposed capital gains tax concessions to investments made in eligible innovative start-up companies where investors subscribe for newly issued equity through an initial public offering (IPO) or subsequent secondary capital raising where all other eligibility criteria are satisfied. Australia&#39;s public markets play an important role in funding early-stage and high-potential growth companies seeking to scale their businesses. The proposed reforms should be designed to support investment in early stage and innovative companies required for the commercialisation and scale up phases of their development regardless of whether capital is raised through private or public markets.</td><td> </td></tr></tbody></table>

        
    </div>
    
    

</div>
</div>


    
    
    <div class="banner-component"><div class="accordion">
    <div class="accordion__item">
        <div class="accordion__item__header beforeBorder" role="accordion" tabindex="0">
            <i class="asx-icon-up gtm-accordion"></i>
            <h6 class="gtm-accordion">2025</h6>
        </div>
        <div class="accordion__item__body hidden">

            


<div class="aem-Grid aem-Grid--12 aem-Grid--default--12 ">
    
    <div class="table-component aem-GridColumn aem-GridColumn--default--12">
 
  <div class="table-container paddingtop15  normalTable">
    
    <div data-table-fix-col="0" data-table-fix-row="0" class="rebrand-datatables  ''">
        
            <table width="100%" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="1" border="0"><tbody><tr><td width="10%"><b>Date</b></td><td><b>Description</b></td></tr><tr><td>28/04/25</td><td>ASX made a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2025/asx-submission-opportunities-to-support-australian-listed-markets.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">submission</a> to ASIC’s discussion paper on the dynamics between public and private markets. ASX’s submission outlined a number of opportunities to make it easier and faster for local and international companies to list in Australia.</td></tr></tbody></table>

        
    </div>
    
    

</div>
</div>

    
</div>

        </div>
    
        <div class="accordion__item__header beforeBorder" role="accordion" tabindex="0">
            <i class="asx-icon-up gtm-accordion"></i>
            <h6 class="gtm-accordion">2024</h6>
        </div>
        <div class="accordion__item__body hidden">

            


<div class="aem-Grid aem-Grid--12 aem-Grid--default--12 ">
    
    <div class="table-component aem-GridColumn aem-GridColumn--default--12">
 
  <div class="table-container paddingtop15  normalTable">
    
    <div data-table-fix-col="0" data-table-fix-row="0" class="rebrand-datatables  ''">
        
            <table border="0" cellpadding="1" cellspacing="0" width="100%"><tbody><tr><td width="10%"><b>Date</b></td><td><b>Description</b></td></tr><tr><td>18/09/24</td><td>On 18 September 2024, ASX made a <a target="_blank" href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2024/asx-submission-asic-cp-379-cs-services-rules.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer">submission</a> to ASIC&#39;s Consultation Paper CP379 relating to draft ASIC CS Services Rules. ASX&#39;s submission included suggestions for clarification for how the rules are intended to operate and commented on the proposed transition period. The submission also provided feedback on ensuring an appropriate balance between achieving ASIC’s stated policy intention and minimising unnecessary additional compliance costs.</td></tr><tr><td>06/06/24</td><td>On 6 June 2024, ASX made a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2024/asx-response-to-transmission-access-reform-consultation-paper.pdf">submission</a> to the Australian Energy Market Commission&#39;s consultation on Transmission Access Reform. The submission focused on a question in the consultation paper relating to the impact of the proposed hybrid model on financial markets. </td></tr><tr><td>15/05/24</td><td>On 15 May 2024, ASX made a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2024/asx-submission-to-inquiry-into-wholesale-investor-and-wholesale-client-tests.pdf">submission</a> to the Parliamentary Joint Committee Inquiry into the wholesale investor and wholesale client tests. The ASX submission encouraged the Committee to consider potential impacts on the ability for issuers to raise capital and on investment diversity for investors when contemplating any changes. </td></tr><tr><td>12/04/24</td><td>On 12 April 2024, ASX made a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2024/asx-submission-senate-inquiry-into-tlab-financial-market-infrastructure-and-other-measures.pdf">submission</a> to the Senate Economics Legislation Committee Inquiry on Treasury Laws Amendment (Financial Market Infrastructure and Other Measures) Bill 2024 which reiterated support for the Bill, and detailed our constructive engagement to date on the financial market infrastructure reforms.</td></tr><tr><td>22/04/24</td><td>On 22 April 2024, ASX made a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2024/asx-pjc-submission-20240422.pdf">submission</a> to the Parliamentary Joint Committee on Corporations and Financial Services’ inquiry into the ‘Oversight of ASIC, the Takeovers Panel and the Corporations Legislation’ in relation to ASX’s CHESS replacement project.</td></tr><tr><td valign="top" width="126"><p>29/02/24</p>
</td><td valign="top" width="440"><p>On 29 February 2024, ASX provided a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2024/asx-submission-cics-ministerial-instrument-20240229.pdf">submission</a> to the Treasury consultation on the draft legislative instruments determining the scope of application of the yet to be released ASIC CS services rules and the arbitration regime under the competition in clearing and settlement legislation. ASX’s submission notes that the definition of ‘cash equity’ in the instrument is aligned with industry’s understanding of the term. It also suggests that the explanatory materials should include an explanation of the matters taken into account by the Minister in making the instrument (as required by the legislation), and that a mechanism for review/amendment of the instrument should be clearly articulated.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td valign="top" width="126"><p>09/02/24</p>
</td><td valign="top" width="440"><p>On 9 February, ASX made a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2024/asx-submission-climate-related-financial-disclosure-20240209.pdf">submission</a> to Treasury’s consultation on exposure draft legislation mandating climate-related financial disclosures. ASX is supportive of the proposed reforms, but notes risks with the current proposed start date of 1 July 2024 and suggests that at least a 12 month transition period be provided.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>09/02/24</td><td>On 9 February 2024, ASX made a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2024/asx-submission-fmi-reforms-20240209.pdf">submission</a> to Treasury’s consultation on draft legislation relating to Financial Market Infrastructure Regulatory Reforms. ASX’s submission is broadly supportive of the reforms, noting that the changes will bring Australia into alignment with international counterparts. The submission covers a number of technical issues intended to achieve better outcomes consistent with the policy intent articulated by the Government.</td></tr><tr><td valign="top" width="126"><p>19/01/24</p>
</td><td valign="top" width="440"><p>On 19 January 2024, ASX made a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2024/asx-submission-fss-application-to-sffs-20240119.pdf">submission</a> to the RBA’s consultation on increasing the threshold for the application of the Financial Stability Standards for Securities Settlement Facilities (SSFs) from $200 million to $40 billion in annual value of settled financial obligations.</p>
</td></tr></tbody></table>

        
    </div>
    
    

</div>
</div>

    
</div>

        </div>
    
        <div class="accordion__item__header beforeBorder" role="accordion" tabindex="0">
            <i class="asx-icon-up gtm-accordion"></i>
            <h6 class="gtm-accordion">2023</h6>
        </div>
        <div class="accordion__item__body hidden">

            


<div class="aem-Grid aem-Grid--12 aem-Grid--default--12 ">
    
    <div class="table-component aem-GridColumn aem-GridColumn--default--12">
 
  <div class="table-container   normalTable">
    
    <div data-table-fix-col="0" data-table-fix-row="0" class="rebrand-datatables  ''">
        
            <table width="100%" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="1" border="0"><tbody><tr><td width="10%"><b>Date</b></td><td><b>Description</b></td></tr><tr><td width="127" valign="top"><p>8/12/23</p>
</td><td width="439" valign="top"><p>On 8 December 2023, ASX made a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/asx-submission-review-of-changes-to-continuous-disclosure-20231208.pdf">submission</a> to Treasury’s review of changes to the continuous disclosure regime. While ASX considers it too soon to fully observe the impact of the 2021 Amendments, in the interests of ensuring the effectiveness of Australia’s continuous disclosure regime and the integrity and attractiveness of Australian markets, ASX submitted that the 2021 Amendments as they relate to regulator-initiated civil penalty proceedings should be repealed. Regulator action is the primary enforcement mechanism under the continuous disclosure regime and plays a critical role in incentivising robust disclosure practices by listed entities. The submission also sets out that the 2021 Amendments as they relate to private plaintiff-initiated civil penalty proceedings should remain, unless evidence becomes available that demonstrates a detrimental impact on the disclosure practices of entities. Requiring the demonstration of fault on the part of the disclosing entity for a successful private plaintiff-initiated action may reduce incentives for potential plaintiffs to pursue ‘opportunistic’ actions.<b></b></p>
</td></tr><tr><td width="127" valign="top"><p>6/10/23</p>
</td><td width="439" valign="top"><p>On 6 October 2023, ASX made a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/asx-submission-managed-investment-scheme-review-20231006.pdf">submission</a> to Treasury’s review of the regulatory framework for managed investment schemes. The submission explained the interactions between the regulatory framework for managed investment schemes and the process for admission to ASX markets.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td width="127" valign="top"><p>8/9/23</p>
</td><td width="439" valign="top"><p>On 8 September 2023, ASX made a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/asx-submission-fssps-exposure-draft-20230908.pdf">submission</a> to Treasury’s consultation on exposure draft legislation for licensing exemptions for foreign financial service providers.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td width="127" valign="top"><p>28/7/23</p>
</td><td width="439" valign="top"><p>On 28 July 2023, ASX made a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/asx-submission-second-climate-related-financial-disclosure-consultation-20230728.pdf">submission</a> to Treasury’s second consultation on climate-related financial disclosure. The submission indicated support for implementation of mandatory climate-related financial reporting in Australia, noting that accurate and meaningful disclosures in this space will increase investor confidence and strengthen Australia’s position in the international financial landscape. The submission raised concerns with the ambitious timeline for implementation, as a rushed implementation could compromise the effectiveness of the regime.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td>20/04/23</td><td>On 20 April 2023, ASX made a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/asx-submission-to-consultation-on-exposure-draft-legislation-for-competition-in-clearing-and-settlement.pdf">submission</a> to a Treasury consultation on the exposure draft legislation relating to competition in the provision of clearing and settlement services. The submission is supportive of the policy objectives of the draft legislation and sets out some suggested refinements to help ensure the legislation achieves the Government’s intent.</td></tr><tr><td width="127" valign="top"><p>3/3/23</p>
</td><td width="439" valign="top"><p>On 3 March 2023, ASX made a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2023/asx-submission-climate-related-financial-disclosure-consultation-20230303.pdf">submission</a> to Treasury’s consultation on climate related financial disclosure. ASX’s submission is broadly supportive of the proposal, and submitted that disclosure obligations should not be limited to large listed companies and should apply to both large listed and large unlisted companies.</p>
</td></tr></tbody></table>

        
    </div>
    
    

</div>
</div>

</td><td width="439" valign="top"><p>On 1 December 2022, ASX made a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/asx-submission-alrc-corps-interim-report-b-20221201.pdf">submission</a> to the Australian Law Review Commission’s Review of the Legislative Framework for Corporations and Financial Services Regulation Interim Report B.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td width="127" valign="top"><p>15/11/22</p>
</td><td width="439" valign="top"><p>On 15 November 2022, ASX made a <a href="/content/dam/asx/about/regulations/public-consultations/2022/asx-submission-asic-ifm-review-20221115.pdf">submission</a> to Treasury’s review of the ASIC Industry Funding Model.</p>
